Upon notice, learned State Counsel raises no objection in case the present application is allowed and the main appeal is taken up today itself.
In view of the above and with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, present application is allowed and the main appeal is taken up today itself.
MAIN APPEAL

Present appeal has been preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act"), to modify the award dated 26.08.2014 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Pathankot (hereinafter to be referred as "Reference Court") seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

[2] Briefly, the facts are that in pursuance of Punjab Govt. Notification dated 16.06.1994 issued under Section 4 of the Act, followed by Notification dated 28.10.1994 issued under Section 6 thereof, the land of appellant, situated in the revenue estate of Village Kot Khas, Tehsil Pathankot, District Gurdaspur (now Pathankot), for setting up Shahpur Kandi Dam, was acquired.

At the time of acquisition of land, certain fruit bearing trees as well as non-fruit bearing trees existed over the same and a separate Award No. 16 dated 04.12.1996 was passed by the Land Acquisition Collector (for short "LAC") in exercise of its powers under Section 11 of the Act in this regard.

[3] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons, including the appellant, filed objections under Section 18 of the Act, which were decided /
allowed vide Award dated 26.08.2014 by Reference Court, whereby the landowners were held 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:163155 entitled for increase of 4.9% over and above the value assessed by the LAC.
[4] Aggrieved thereof, the appellant preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount, which stood admitted vide order dated 01.05.2015 by this Court.

[5] It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant- appellant that present appeal is squarely covered with the judgment dated 29.07.2024 rendered by this Court in CM No. 5380-CI of 2023 in/and RFA No. 738 of 2015, titled "Jaswant Singh Versus State of Punjab and others", arising out of the same notification, vide which the land of appellant had been acquired.

sentences.text: [8] From the records, it is apparent that the present appeal is squarely covered with the judgment dated 29.07.2024 passed in case of Jaswant Singh (supra), which is arising out of the same acquisition / Notification dated 16.06.1994 issued under Section 4 of the Act, covering the same revenue estate of Village Kot Khas, Tehsil Pathankot, District Gurdaspur (now Pathankot), whereby the landowner has been held entitled for increase of 170% over and above the amount assessed by the LAC vide its award dated 04.12.1996 towards compensation for the fruit bearing as well as non- fruit trees.

For reference, relevant para-9 of the judgment dated 29.07.2024 passed in case of Jaswant Singh (supra) reads as under:-
3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:163155 " 9.

Accordingly, in view of the discussion made hereinabove, the impugned award dated 26.08.2014, passed by the Reference Court is set aside and the present appeal is allowed to the extent that based on the appreciation of price index between 1985 to 1994, the appellant-landowner shall be entitled for increase of 170% over and above the amount assessed by the Land Acquisition Collector vide its award dated 04.12.1996 towards compensation for the fruit bearing as well as non-fruit bearing trees besides all other statutory benefits and interests provided as admissible under the 1894 Act. "

[9] Based upon the above, applying the principle of parity, besides award of just and fair compensation, the landowner / appellant being similarly situated is held entitled for grant of similar amount of compensation as has been awarded to other landowner vide judgment dated 29.07.2024 in case of Jaswant Singh (supra), alongwith all other statutory benefits and interest thereupon as provided under the Act.
[10] Accordingly, the present appeal is disposed off in terms of order dated 29.07.2024 passed in Jaswant Singh's case (supra).
[11] Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand(s) disposed off.
December 05, 2024 ( HARKESH MANUJA )
'dk kamra' JUDGE
